basic_info: Alan, male, age approx. late 30s to early 40s, chief complaint: left shoulder pain for 3 weeks, affecting arm movement and sleep.
present_illness: Onset 3 weeks ago, persistent dull, aching pain localized to the left shoulder, affecting daily activities and sleep. No chest pain, shortness of breath, or numbness in the arm. No history of trauma, but recent repetitive strain from basement work (e.g., ceiling installation). The patient reports trouble moving the arm, especially when lifting or reaching overhead, which causes significant pain. The arm feels weak when used, but grip strength is preserved. No clicking, popping, or locking in the shoulder. No prior shoulder injuries or surgeries. The patient reports that the pain is worse at night, especially when trying to sleep, and often wakes him up. He has not experienced any clicking, popping, or locking in the shoulder. He has not had any recent imaging studies or consultations with a healthcare provider regarding this shoulder pain. This is the first time he is seeing a doctor about it. The patient also reports experiencing weakness in the left arm, especially when lifting or reaching overhead, and has difficulty finding a comfortable sleeping position due to the pain. He has not experienced any fatigue, weight loss, or fever in the past few weeks. The patient reports stiffness in the left shoulder, especially in the morning or after resting, which makes it difficult to move the shoulder smoothly. It feels stuck initially before movement becomes easier. This stiffness is contributing to the limitation in daily activities and sleep. The patient states that lifting anything or reaching overhead definitely makes the pain worse, and the only thing that seems to relieve it a little is resting, but even then, the pain is still present, especially at night. The patient also reports that the pain is pretty constant and has been getting worse over time, especially at night when trying to sleep.
past_history: No history of repetitive strain or overuse reported. No history of inflammatory or autoimmune conditions. No prior shoulder injuries or surgeries. No history of shoulder dislocation or subluxation reported.
physical_exam: Vital signs: BP 120/80 mmHg, HR 72 bpm, Temp 36.8°C. Shoulder examination: No visible swelling, redness, or warmth. Range of motion is limited, especially with abduction and external rotation. Mild tenderness over the anterior aspect of the shoulder. No neurological deficits noted.
aux_exam: Imaging studies: None reported. Consultations: None reported.
